answer_1.quote: We use a BART‑based sequence‑to‑sequence model to represent the distribution of valid conclusion statements conditioned on one or more premise statements …
answer_1.outputs: Generated natural language conclusions (deductions) from premise sentences

answer_2.quote: We also compute the perplexity of reference conclusions under each model … For the perturbation sets, we also report the BLEURT score of generated conclusions with respect to reference conclusions.

answer_4.quote: We evaluate model performance on each dataset primarily through a manual assessment of conclusion validity. The first author placed generated conclusions into one of six categories: Valid, Valid with minor grammar errors, Repeats premises, Unsupported, Incompatible, Incomprehensible.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators (first author, with re‑annotation by the last author) labeled each generated conclusion according to predefined categories indicating validity and grammaticality.
